headline: The Q8 bridge's 1,179,648 objectwise equivariant bijections and the full-Clifford Fourier compiler's six character-to-sheet assignments are different object types, not a before/after subset census. The complete full-Clifford intertwiner space has dimension seven. Within the Fourier ansatz there are exactly 3! assignments of the three C3 characters to the certified beta=0,1,2 sheets. Requiring beta=0 to carry the trivial character leaves (0,1,2) and (0,2,1), exchanged by complex conjugation. Real E6 cubic signs and integer Qpsi data cannot distinguish that pair.

selector_verdict.needed_next_observable: a genuinely mu3-oriented phase/holonomy/chirality datum with a fixed orientation convention

boundary: The six assignments classify a discrete choice inside the induced/Fourier ansatz; they are not the whole seven-dimensional full-Clifford intertwiner space and are not a subset reduction of the Q8 objectwise gauges. The final two assignments need not be physically equivalent; the certified real and integer observables simply cannot distinguish them.
